title: Natural-image response spectra decayed faster in higher mouse visual areas in Allen Neuropixels (32 mice) and two-photon (193 mice) data after reliability, layer and Cre-line controls
abstract: We asked if the geometry of visual population codes changes along the connectivity-defined mouse visual hierarchy. We used responses to the same 118 natural images in Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels data (32 mice, 11,559 units in LGd, LP and six cortical areas) and Allen Visual Coding two-photon data (193 mice, 38,466 excitatory cells in six cortical areas). For each area we calculated cross-validated PCA spectra and fitted the decay exponent alpha over ranks 2 to 30. We compared alpha with the anatomical hierarchy score of Harris et al. (2019). In Neuropixels populations of 300 units, alpha was 0.67 in LGd, 0.81 in VISp and 0.96 in VISam (Spearman rho 0.88 over 8 structures; slope 0.27 per hierarchy unit, 95% mouse bootstrap 0.15 to 0.34; cortex only 0.20, 0.08 to 0.29). Two-photon data agreed: alpha 0.61 in VISp and 1.11 in VISam, slope 0.55 (0.31 to 0.78), and 0.54 (0.38 to 0.69) inside 12 Cre-line and depth strata. The slope stayed positive after reliability matching, inside fixed reliability bands, after a simulation-based bias correction, in a 50-250 ms window, and inside CCF cortical layers (0.39, 0.19 to 0.54). Thus higher areas put more reliable image variance into fewer dimensions. Limitations: 118 images bias alpha low by about 0.09 and the spectra are curved, so alpha depends on the fit range; ranks 1 to 10 showed no cortical trend. Inside single mice, 20 to 30 units gave no clear cortical slope. The test is correlational over only 6 to 8 areas, and receptive-field size and position were not controlled. Code, aggregate results, figures and exact data provenance are included; Allen data files stay external.
